**In one line**: Computerworld reports that the EU is investigating OpenAI and Anthropic following incidents involving AI agents.

### Key points
- The probe targets two leading frontier AI developers, **OpenAI** and **Anthropic**.
- It was reportedly triggered by incidents involving **AI agents**, meaning autonomous systems that carry out tasks on a user's behalf.
- The specific incidents, the scope of the inquiry and its legal basis are not yet clear from available details. See the original report for specifics.
- The investigation comes as the EU implements its AI Act, which places obligations on providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models.

### Why it matters
AI regulation has so far focused mostly on what models say. This probe suggests regulators may now also scrutinize what AI systems **do**. Companies shipping or adopting agentic products should review their incident-response processes and how responsibility is assigned before oversight tightens.
